classification.difficultyReason: Reduce two exponential equations to simultaneous linear equations using common bases, then solve by elimination or substitution.

content.prompt: Solve each set of simultaneous equations.

answer.short:
$x=3,\ y=5$

Express each equation with a common base, then solve the resulting linear equations.
answer.worked:
Using bases 3 and 2 respectively:
$$\begin{align*}3^{2x}&=3^{3y-9}\\2^{4x+4}&=2^{3y+1}\end{align*}$$
Equating indices gives
$$\begin{align*}2x-3y&=-9\qquad(1)\\4x-3y&=-3\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Subtract (1) from (2):
$$\begin{align*}2x&=6\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (1):
$$\begin{align*}6-3y&=-9\\-3y&=-15\\y&=5\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=5,\ y=2$

Express each equation with a common base, then solve the resulting linear equations.
answer.worked:
Using bases 2 and 5 respectively:
$$\begin{align*}2^{3x}&=2^{5y+5}\\5^{x-1}&=5^{2y}\end{align*}$$
Equating indices gives
$$\begin{align*}3x-5y&=5\qquad(1)\\x-2y&=1\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Multiply (2) by 3, then subtract (1):
$$\begin{align*}3x-6y&=3\\-y&=-2\\y&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}x-4&=1\\x&=5\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=-\frac{63}{8},\ y=-\frac94$

Express each equation with a common base, then eliminate $x$.
answer.worked:
Using bases 7 and 2 respectively:
$$\begin{align*}7^{2x+6}&=7^{3y-3}\\2^{x+y}&=2^{3x-6y}\end{align*}$$
Equating indices gives
$$\begin{align*}2x+6&=3y-3\\x+y&=3x-6y\end{align*}$$
Rearrange:
$$\begin{align*}2x-3y&=-9\qquad(1)\\2x-7y&=0\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Subtract (2) from (1):
$$\begin{align*}4y&=-9\\y&=-\frac94\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}2x&=7\left(-\frac94\right)\\2x&=-\frac{63}{4}\\x&=-\frac{63}{8}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$x=2,\ y=3$

Express each equation with a common base, then solve the resulting linear equations.
answer.worked:
Using bases 2 and 7 respectively:
$$\begin{align*}2^{3x}&=2^{2y}\\7^{3x+3}&=7^{3y}\end{align*}$$
Equating indices and simplifying gives
$$\begin{align*}3x-2y&=0\qquad(1)\\x-y&=-1\qquad(2)\end{align*}$$
Subtract twice (2) from (1):
$$\begin{align*}x&=2\end{align*}$$
Substitute into (2):
$$\begin{align*}2-y&=-1\\y&=3\end{align*}$$
